Act 1

⏳ was & were

🦢
Hello, Vasilisa! Today we get into a time machine and travel to the past. In the past, «am» and «is» become «was», and «are» becomes «were».
was / wasn't
I, he, she, it
Balanchine was born in St Petersburg.
The exam wasn't easy.
were / weren't
you, we, they
Nureyev and Fonteyn were partners.
Were you nervous? No, I wasn't.
Запомни: «я родилась» по-английски I was born. «Там было много людей»: There were a lot of people.

Write was, wasn't, were or weren't

Впиши сама, вариантов на выбор нет. (not) значит, что нужно отрицание. Можно писать полную форму: was not.

+ edstart → started
+ ddance → danced
hope → hoped
согласная + y → iedstudy → studied
cry → cried
гласная + y → yedplay → played
stay → stayed
двойная букваstop → stopped
plan → planned
ударение в концеprefer → preferred

Act 4

🌟 Legends of ballet

🦢
Guess what, Vasilisa! Almost all these legends studied at YOUR school in St Petersburg. Some of them stayed in Russia, and some changed ballet in London and New York.

Прочитай истории. Потом нажми «Покажи глаголы»: подсветятся все глаголы в прошедшем времени.

Russian legends
🇷🇺

Agrippina Vaganova

1879 to 1951

Agrippina Vaganova was born in St Petersburg in 1879. She studied at the Imperial Ballet School, and in 1897 she began to dance at the Mariinsky Theatre. People called her «the queen of variations». Later she left the stage and became a teacher. From 1921 she taught at her old ballet school, and many of her students became stars. In 1934 she wrote a famous book about classical dance. She died in 1951, and in 1957 the school got her name. Yes, it is your school!

🩰

Vaslav Nijinsky

1889 to 1950

Vaslav Nijinsky was born in Kyiv in 1889 or 1890: nobody knows the exact year! He studied at the Imperial Ballet School in St Petersburg and danced at the Mariinsky Theatre. Then he went to Paris, and the audience there loved him. He was famous for his amazing jumps. In 1911 he danced Petrushka, and in 1912 he made his own ballet, The Afternoon of a Faun. He died in London in 1950.

🇷🇺

Galina Ulanova

1910 to 1998

Galina Ulanova was born in St Petersburg in 1910. Her first teacher was her mother, and then she studied with Agrippina Vaganova herself! In 1928 she began to dance at the Mariinsky Theatre. One of her most famous roles was Juliet in Prokofiev's Romeo and Juliet. In 1944 she moved to the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow, and in 1945 she danced Cinderella in the very first performance of Prokofiev's new ballet. She left the stage when she was fifty.

🇷🇺

Maya Plisetskaya

1925 to 2015

Maya Plisetskaya was born in Moscow in 1925. She started at the Bolshoi ballet school when she was nine, and in 1943 she joined the Bolshoi Ballet. She was famous for Swan Lake and The Dying Swan. In 1967 she danced Carmen in a new ballet, Carmen Suite, and Carmen became her favourite role. She didn't want to stop: she danced The Dying Swan even in her late sixties! She died in 2015.

From Russia to London and New York
🇺🇸

George Balanchine

1904 to 1983

George Balanchine was born in St Petersburg in 1904. When he was nine, he entered the Imperial Ballet School. Today this school is the Vaganova Academy! In 1924 he left Russia and worked in Europe. In 1933 he came to America. A year later, he opened the School of American Ballet in New York, and in 1948 he started New York City Ballet. He made more than 400 ballets. In 1954 he created his own Nutcracker, and he danced the role of Drosselmeyer himself!

🇬🇧

The Royal Ballet

since 1931

In 1931 Ninette de Valois started a small ballet company in London. It was called the Vic-Wells Ballet. In 1946 the company moved to the Royal Opera House in Covent Garden. In 1956 it got a new name: The Royal Ballet. Its biggest star was Margot Fonteyn. She danced with the company all her life.

🇬🇧

Rudolf Nureyev

1938 to 1993

Rudolf Nureyev was born on a train in 1938. He loved dance, but he started at the Vaganova school very late: he was seventeen! He worked very hard, and in 1958 he joined the Kirov Ballet. In 1961, on a tour in Paris, he decided not to go back home. In 1962 he danced Giselle with Margot Fonteyn in London. She was nineteen years older than him, but they became the most famous partners in ballet.

🇺🇸

Mikhail Baryshnikov

born in 1948

Mikhail Baryshnikov was born in Riga in 1948. In 1964 he entered the Vaganova school, and in 1967 he joined the Kirov Ballet. In 1974, on a tour in Canada, he decided to stay in the West. He danced with American Ballet Theatre and with New York City Ballet, where he worked with Balanchine. From 1980 to 1989 he was the director of American Ballet Theatre. He also acted in films.

entered: поступил · stage: сцена · company: труппа · tour: гастроли · joined: пришел в труппу · audience: зрители · partners: партнеры · director: художественный руководитель
В те годы Петербург назывался Ленинградом, а театр Кирова сегодня снова Мариинский. Нуреев поступил в училище в 17 лет, очень поздно для балета, и все равно стал звездой мира.

Act 6

❓ Questions & negatives

did + глагол без -ed
Did he dance? Yes, he did. / No, he didn't.
He didn't go home. (не didn't went!)
was / were
Was she Russian? Yes, she was.
Were they partners? No, they weren't.

1. Short answers

Впиши короткий ответ одним словом: did, didn't, was, wasn't, were или weren't.

2. Make it negative

Впиши отрицание: didn't + глагол. Например: I saw Giselle. → I didn't see Swan Lake.

Act 8

🩰 Then & now: Hailey Bieber

Не только звезды балета мечтали о сцене. Прочитай историю Хейли Бибер.

Hailey Bieber is a famous model. She is married to the singer Justin Bieber. But when she was a little girl, she wanted to be a ballerina! As a teenager, she studied ballet at American Ballet Theatre in New York in the summer. Then she hurt her foot, and she stopped dancing. Later, she became a model. She says: «I used to be a ballet dancer». Ballet still inspires her today.

married to: замужем за · teenager: подросток · hurt her foot: повредила стопу · used to be: раньше была · inspires: вдохновляет
